sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Co-IP with FLAG-Gal-8 confirmed HA-LILRB4 retains Gal-8 binding; function preserved.
sites.rationale: LILRB4 is a type I single-pass TM protein (SP residues 1-21, EC 22-259, TM 260-280, IC 281-448). L1 reports a full-length HA-tagged construct with no residue named; because exactly one terminus is extracellular, the junction is unambiguously after the SP cleavage site (insert_after_residue=21, placing the tag before the mature Q22). Python confirms residue 21='M' and residue 22='Q'. The tag position is 238 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of any structural constraint. The co-IP with Gal-8 (an extracellular LILRB4 ligand) demonstrates the tagged protein folds, traffics to the membrane, and retains ligand-binding function. Full-length HA-tagged LILRB4 expressed in HEK293 cells; co-immunoprecipitated with FLAG-tagged Galectin-8, demonstrating membrane-anchored expression and retained extracellular ligand binding.

sources.claim: (H) Immune blotting of coimmunoprecipitation of FLAG-tagged Gal-8 and hemagglutinin (HA)-tagged LILRB4.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. It reports a full-length HA-tagged LILRB4 with no residue number; the N-terminal extracellular position is topology-derived as the sole extracellular terminus. The C-terminus (residue 448) is intracellular and was not considered as a surface site. No internal loop insertions are supported by the ledger.
